content.text:
What kind of story is Treasure Island?

Treasure Island is a classic adventure in which a boy named Jim Hawkins gets hold of a treasure map, sets sail on a voyage, and, among pirates, protects the treasure with courage and wisdom. With its nail-biting voyage and pirate tale, adventure-loving children get deeply drawn in.

content.text:
Stevenson's original story

"Treasure Island" is an adventure novel published in 1883 by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson. With captivating characters like the one-legged pirate Long John Silver and a setting of a treasure map and a deserted island, it became the archetype for countless pirate stories that followed.

content.alt: Treasure Island - Treasure Island plot summary
content.text:
Treasure Island plot summary

Having come upon a treasure map by chance at an inn, Jim sets sail for Treasure Island together with the grown-ups. But it turns out that many of the sailors are pirates after the treasure. At each dangerous moment Jim judges calmly and finds his courage, and in the end he safely protects the treasure and returns home.

content.alt: Treasure Island - The lessons of Treasure Island
content.text:
The lessons of Treasure Island

Treasure Island shows that when you think calmly and find your courage even in the face of danger, a way opens up. You can also talk about the wisdom to tell apart people whose true intentions are unknowable even when they seem kind, and the value of promises and trust.

content.alt: Treasure Island - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Make sound effects for the waves and wind by sweeping your hand across the desk, and act out the pirates' lines in a deep, rough voice to boost immersion. In the crisis scenes, ask, "What will Jim do now?" so your child can come up with solutions. Afterward, it's lovely to move on to an activity of drawing your own treasure map. Suitable for ages 5-7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Treasure Island good for?
A. It's suitable for ages 5-7. With many scene changes and a big adventure scale, it's especially enjoyed by children who love adventure.

Q. Won't the pirates be scary?
A. The picture book for young children depicts the pirates as non-threatening, and the satisfying ending lets children watch with peace of mind.

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Activities like drawing a treasure map, making paper boats, and tracing the sea route on a world map are great.
